title: EventHandler
description: A registered binding, declared in or against a data store, that attaches to a collection or database scope and runs an action automatically when specified data-change events or data conditions occur there (SQL trigger, change-stream or CDC subscription, keyspace notification, watcher or alert rule). It is the activation wiring (event, timing, granularity, filter), not the computation body it invokes. Use StoredLogic instead when the symbol is the function, procedure, Lua script or pipeline body that does the work (e.g. the trigger function created by CREATE FUNCTION ... RETURNS trigger), not the declaration that binds it to events. Use ValidationRule instead when integrity is enforced declaratively by the engine (CHECK, NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY, JSON Schema validator) rather than by a BEFORE trigger that runs code to reject or rewrite rows. Use RetentionPolicy instead when the mechanism is a TTL, ILM or downsampling policy that expires or moves data by age, rather than reacting to individual insert, update, delete or expiry events with custom logic. Use View instead when derived data is kept current by a materialized view or continuous aggregate refresh policy rather than by a handler that writes to another collection on each change.

handlerType.description: Type of event handler mechanism. TRIGGER: synchronous SQL trigger (BEFORE/AFTER DML). CHANGE_STREAM: asynchronous document change feed (MongoDB, CouchDB). CDC_LISTENER: change data capture consumer (Cassandra, Debezium). KEYSPACE_NOTIFICATION: key event notification (Redis). STREAM_PROCESSOR: stream-based event processor (Redis Streams, Kafka Connect). WATCHER: periodic condition check and alert (Elasticsearch). ALERT_RULE: threshold or anomaly alerting (time-series, monitoring). CUSTOM: engine-specific mechanism not listed.

targetCollection.description: The collection or database-level scope this handler is attached to.

timing.description: When the handler fires relative to the event. BEFORE: fires before the operation (SQL BEFORE trigger). AFTER: fires after the operation (SQL AFTER trigger). INSTEAD_OF: replaces the operation (SQL INSTEAD OF trigger for views). ON_CHANGE: fires when a change is detected (change streams, CDC). CONTINUOUS: always-on stream processing.

events.description: Events that activate this handler. SQL: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE. Document: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/REPLACE/DROP/INVALIDATE. Key-value: EXPIRE/SET/DEL. Monitoring: THRESHOLD/ANOMALY. CUSTOM: engine-specific event not listed.

granularity.description: Granularity of handler activation. ROW: fires once per affected row (SQL FOR EACH ROW). STATEMENT: fires once per SQL statement. DOCUMENT: fires per changed document (document store change streams). KEY: fires per key operation (key-value notifications). BATCH: fires per batch of changes (CDC, stream processing).

action.description: Reference to the stored logic (function name, pipeline reference, or inline expression) that executes when this handler fires.

condition.description: Optional filter condition. Only events matching this condition activate the handler. Maps to SQL WHEN clause, MongoDB pipeline $match stage, or Elasticsearch watcher condition.

enabled.description: Whether the handler is currently active and will fire; set false when it is declared but disabled (e.g. ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER, a paused connector or deactivated watcher), otherwise true, which is the default.

x-dr-standard: ISO/IEC 9075-2 (SQL/Foundation) <trigger definition> (CREATE TRIGGER), extended to change streams, CDC and keyspace notifications
x-dr-evidence: A migration or DDL file containing CREATE TRIGGER ... BEFORE|AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON <table> FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION <fn>()

Code or config opening a change feed on a store, e.g. MongoDB collection.watch([{ $match: ... }]), a DynamoDB StreamSpecification with a Lambda event source mapping, or a Debezium connector config listing table.include.list
Redis setup issuing CONFIG SET notify-keyspace-events (or notify-keyspace-events in redis.conf) together with a PSUBSCRIBE on __keyspace@*__ or __keyevent@*__ channels
